strategyReview: The weekend funding reversion long family remains profitable overall (244/343 wins, 71% win rate) but current open positions show deep drawdowns, indicating recent regime stress. The one‑touch sell‑YES edge signal has perfect live execution (4/4 wins) but heavy shadow losses suggest edge signals are noisy and heavily dependent on filtering. Funding‑extreme‑short trades are steady with 61% wins but produce minimal net PnL; the signal has been asset‑specific winning for AMZN but struggling for OIL. The big losers are shadow‑mined variants that omit critical contextual filters (weekday, trend, and regime) and rely on absolute thresholds; they account for most of the unrealised pain. The research findings highlight robust edges in informed flow, PM‑IV rich NO setups, and BTC one‑touch NO edges that deserve promotion with careful catalog‑based conditions.

failureClusters.evidence: CBRS (H‑539) 8/18 wins, AAPL (H‑537) 6/14 wins, COIN (H‑538) 1/7 wins – all use simple funding < ‑10 threshold but lack weekend/context filter. Losses occurred when funding deepened or reversed only briefly outside true weekend hours.
failureClusters.recommendation: Mandate a day‑of‑week = [sat, sun] condition and increase funding extremity threshold for these weekend‑funding shadow families.

failureClusters.theme: Gold one‑touch NO edge mispricing fade
failureClusters.evidence: Shadow‑mined GOLD heatmap NO (H‑534) 0/20 wins, predicted >2% spot decline but GOLD rallied sharply. The cap‑edge signal flagged rich NO premiums that persisted while spot kept rising.
failureClusters.recommendation: Only take the sell‑YES edge when the underlying spot is already in a bearish regime (e.g., below its 7‑day SMA) to avoid fading strong uptrends.

failureClusters.theme: Absolute‑threshold PM‑IV expansion fails in low‑vol regimes
failureClusters.evidence: BTC PM‑IV expansion (H‑001) 3/10 wins; after early successes, recent signals produced muted moves (< 2%) as volatility compressed further without a catalyst.
failureClusters.recommendation: Switch to regime‑relative compression (percentile/zscore) and require an oversold condition (spot below SMA) to time the expansion breakout.

failureClusters.evidence: Cross‑asset IV compression family 0/9 wins across multiple variants. The HYPE OI/spot confirmation failed to predict BTC gains; the thesis that HYPE risk‑on reliably precedes BTC breakouts is not holding.
failureClusters.recommendation: Avoid further refinements in this family unless a radically stronger catalyst (e.g., funding extreme + IV compression) can be identified.

newHypotheses.description: Informed‑flow fade: when smart wallets are net short YES (smart_flow_stance ≤ -1) on above‑strike one‑touch contracts with a positive sell‑YES edge, short the asset’s spot. The smart‑money selling on dips and high‑side YES is a reliable contrarian predictor of spot declines.
newHypotheses.prediction: The asset’s spot price will decline >2% within 7 days

newHypotheses.description: GOLD put/call extreme low short: when GOLD’s GLD put/call ratio falls into the bottom 10% of its 7‑day range (indicative of excessive call buying), short GOLD despite the positive trend. Previous positive‑trend filters incorrectly blocked this signal; the extreme low often precedes a corrective pullback.
newHypotheses.prediction: GOLD spot will decline >2% within 3 days

newHypotheses.description: PM‑IV rich NO fade: when Polymarket IV exceeds listed‑option IV by ≥10 vol points on an above‑strike one‑touch NO contract with a positive sell‑YES edge, short the asset. The rich premium on NO contracts points to overpriced downside protection that will compress as spot stabilises or drops modestly.
newHypotheses.prediction: The spot price will decline >2% within 5 days

newHypotheses.description: BTC one‑touch NO edge with moderate strength: when a BTC upside one‑touch NO contract offers a sell‑YES edge between 3 and 8 percentage points and the contract expires within 30 days, short BTC. This captures the cluster where the edge is large enough to compensate for the risk but not so extreme as to indicate a market dislocation that fails to revert.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will decline >2% within 5 days

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑534: Only take the gold one‑touch NO edge when the underlying spot is in a downtrend (below its 7‑day SMA) to avoid fading strong rallies. The cap edge alone is insufficient; a bearish regime context is needed for the mispricing to correct via spot decline.
newHypotheses.prediction: GOLD spot will decline >2% within 3 days

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑539: Restrict CBRS funding reversion to true weekend days (Saturday and Sunday) and require funding deeper than ‑10% to isolate overshoots that rapidly normalise. This aligns with the strong weekend‑only performance seen in the broader WEEKEND_HL_FUNDING_REVERSION_LONG family.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS funding will normalise (increase) and spot will move >2% higher within 2 days as the weekend anomaly corrects

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑537: Apply the same weekend‑only filter and a deeper threshold (<‑15%) to AAPL funding reversion. The evidence shows AAPL funding snap‑backs are concentrated on weekends; weekday signals are false reversals that continue the trend.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL funding will normalise sharply and spot will gain >2% within 2 days

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑001: Shift from absolute PM‑IV thresholds to regime‑relative compression (PM IV below its 20th percentile of 30‑day range) and add an oversold filter (spot below 7‑day SMA) to time the expansion move. This captures genuine cheap‑vol regimes poised for breakouts instead of persistent low‑vol drifting.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will move >2% (abs) within 3 days

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of the cross‑asset IV compression long: add a Bitcoin funding extreme short condition (funding < ‑50%) to identify crowded shorts and require HYPE OI growth >3% to confirm genuine risk‑on capital inflow. This raises the bar for momentum confirmation significantly.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will rise >2% within 5 days as short‑covering and risk‑on inflows combine

hypothesisReviews.observation: All 20 scorable tests failed; GOLD spot did not decline the required >2% in the 2‑day window and instead rallied. The underlying cap edge persisted as gold continued its uptrend, meaning the edge was not a reliable reversal signal.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying-cap edge on gold upside one-touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: CBRS funding < ‑10 produced 44% win rate, with wins concentrated when extreme negative funding snapped back inside a weekend context. Losses occurred when funding was only modestly negative on weekdays and continued to worsen. The primary failure is that simple negative funding without a day‑of‑week filter captures too many regime‑continuation signals.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Deeply negative CBRS funding reliably reverts and leads to a >2% spot gain within 2 days without additional extremity or reversal confirmation.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL funding < ‑10 resulted in 43% win rate, similar to CBRS. Winning instances involved true weekend overshoots, while losses happened when funding settled at ~ ‑10% or worsened on weekdays. The missing weekend filter is the root cause.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative AAPL funding rapidly normalizes and leads to a >2% spot gain without requiring a true tail‑event overshoot.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Early wins captured genuine IV‑driven expansions, but after 23 July the low PM‑IV conditions persisted while spot moved less than 2%, showing that cheap volatility alone is insufficient. The absolute 46/49 thresholds were regime‑stale and did not account for fading implied vol.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC PM IV below 46 while options IV remains high guarantees a >2% absolute spot move within 3 days regardless of trend context.

hypothesisReviews.observation: All nine tests across the cross‑asset IV compression family failed to produce a >2% BTC long move. HYPE OI stability and above‑SMA spot did not confirm continued BTC momentum, indicating the correlation has broken and the conditions are too weak.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC above short‑term trend with HYPE spot above SMA and OI stable confirms a >2% BTC long move over 3‑7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: OIL one‑touch NO edge on heatmap cluster continues to perform well in recent tests (82% win, 9/11 last tests), validating the sell‑YES edge on OIL upside contracts as a reliable short signal when edge exceeds 2 pts and direction is above. The setup family remains robust.

journalEntry: The nightly review confirms that our biggest active risk is open weekend‑funding reversion longs that are deep underwater; while the family historically wins, current conditions are adverse. The key learning is that shadow hypotheses must inherit the filtering logic that made the parent families work — specifically day‑of‑week gates for weekend funding and regime‑relative conditions for volatility and edge signals. We identified that the gold one‑touch NO edge is failing because the edge arises from persistent premiums in a strong trend, so we added a bearish filter. The CBRS/AAPL shadows failed without weekend‑only scope, so we tightened entry accordingly. The PM‑IV expansion family needs regime‑relative compression, not absolute thresholds. The ranked research findings provide several high‑confidence edges, especially informed flow (FIND‑0020) and GOLD put/call extreme (FIND‑0053), which we are now authoring as catalog‑valid hypotheses. No parameter updates are warranted given the lack of evidence for regime‑specific stop/target adjustments.
